method: One-to-one research comparison of 40 existing English/French opening drafts with the corresponding numbered question and answer in the Museo Italian digital transcription. The cross-edition/source, doctrinal, translation, and period-voice approvals are independent later gates; do not infer them from this research pass. Narrower suggested drafts are overlays only, not modifications of original content.
keyWarnings: 1905 digital witness is not authenticated line-by-line to the original printed Vatican edition; Q numbers are transcription locators.
The 1905 prescribed catechism is not a corpus of authenticated personal utterances of Pius X.
Follow-up turns are outside this 40-opening-turn comparison.
Existing pastoral-scruple gates and 1905-versus-current disciplinary qualifiers must remain in force.
Mass Ultra Master Matrix, existing reader, source registries and period-voice pipeline unchanged.
No automatic Chanoine answers, no Denzinger numbers invented, no automatic intent merging.

Q605 says 'words of consecration'; 'Christ's words' relies additionally on Q600/606. Narrow single-Q reply.

suggestedEditorialCorrection.en: At Mass, the conversion takes place at the very moment the priest pronounces the words of consecration.
suggestedEditorialCorrection.fr: À la Messe, la conversion a lieu au moment même où le prêtre prononce les paroles de la consécration.

records.claimScopeObservation: Q607 gives the designation 'transubstantiation'; remaining species belong to Q609–610. Avoid treating adjacent statements as directly in Q607.

suggestedEditorialCorrection.en: The Church calls this miraculous conversion transubstantiation.
suggestedEditorialCorrection.fr: L'Église appelle cette conversion miraculeuse la transsubstantiation.

The original distinguishes continued Real Presence under remaining species from remaining grace; 'gracious indwelling' may invite an overly personalized inference.

suggestedEditorialCorrection.en: After Communion, Christ's Real Presence remains while the sacramental species remain; the Catechism separately says His grace remains unless mortal sin is committed.
suggestedEditorialCorrection.fr: Après la Communion, la Présence réelle du Christ demeure tant que subsistent les espèces sacramentelles ; le Catéchisme distingue sa grâce, qui demeure tant qu'aucun péché mortel n'est commis.

Q652 actually says something sensible is offered and 'destroyed in some manner'. The draft replaces this with 'change or destruction', a substantive alteration of the historical wording.

suggestedEditorialCorrection.en: This historical Catechism describes sacrifice in general as offering something perceptible to God and destroying it in some manner, in acknowledgment of His supreme dominion.
suggestedEditorialCorrection.fr: Ce Catéchisme historique décrit en général le sacrifice comme l'offrande à Dieu d'une chose sensible, détruite d'une certaine manière, pour reconnaître sa souveraine domination.

Q655 states the same Christ is offered and the manner differs; the formula 'same Priest and Victim' draws on wider sacrificial theology and Q660, not only Q655.

suggestedEditorialCorrection.en: The sacrifice of the Mass is substantially the same as that of the Cross because the same Jesus Christ is offered through the ministry of priests; the manner of offering differs, while their essential relation remains.
suggestedEditorialCorrection.fr: Le sacrifice de la Messe est substantiellement le même que celui de la Croix, puisque le même Jésus-Christ est offert par le ministère des prêtres ; le mode d'offrande diffère, mais le lien essentiel demeure.

Q657 speaks of the visible representation of Blood-shedding through the distinct species, and separately explains full presence by concomitance and hypostatic union. 'Separate consecration' is an interpretation rather than the source's own wording.

suggestedEditorialCorrection.en: The Mass visibly represents Christ's Blood-shedding through the distinct Eucharistic species; nevertheless the whole living Christ is present under either species, as the Catechism explains.
suggestedEditorialCorrection.fr: La Messe représente sensiblement l'effusion du Sang du Christ par les espèces eucharistiques distinctes ; néanmoins, le Christ vivant tout entier est présent sous chacune d'elles, comme l'explique le Catéchisme.
